artifact.name: followup-03-root-publication
artifact.campaign: read-only root publication and lifecycle follow-up
artifact.subject: NOUN-STAR-ROOT-PUBLICATION-AND-LIFECYCLE

scope.excluded_scope: No source implementation, runtime experiment, game-directory inspection, spore.db query, or historical edit was performed. Prior dossiers were not counted as fresh binary evidence.
scope.requested_question: Can noun/star root pointer equality and publication be closed statically, or what exact lower bound remains?

static_observations: Direct xref enumeration for each root word and each accessor
Read-only global audits and four-byte memory reads
Exact four-byte literal scans for each root word
Read-only P-code constant/address propagation scan for computed target stores
Table/base inspection around 0x0167ea80 and the star-getter thunk
Accessor co-call scan and decompilation of co-call functions
Constructor, initialization, shutdown, destructor, noun-map erase, and noun-record cleanup inspection
limitations: A failed direct or bounded computed search is not proof that an indirect writer, bulk copy, opaque helper, loader write, or runtime publication does not exist.
The computed scan tracks concrete P-code arithmetic only; it does not resolve values loaded through opaque pointers, external calls, or opaque bulk memory operations.
The loaded image has zero bytes at all four target words, so static memory state cannot distinguish unpublished, cleared, or runtime-published states.

root_words.name: DAT_0167eae0
root_words.accessor_contract: Raw borrowed pointer load; no validation, allocation, AddRef, Release, lock, or ownership transfer.

root_words.name: DAT_0167eb60
root_words.accessor_contract: Raw borrowed pointer load; no validation, allocation, AddRef, Release, lock, or ownership transfer.

root_words.name: DAT_0167eae4
root_words.accessor_contract: The primary accessor is a raw borrowed load. 0x00b3d2c0 is a state-selected relationship bridge, not a root publisher.

root_words.name: DAT_0167eb0c
root_words.accessor_contract: Raw borrowed pointer load; no validation, allocation, AddRef, Release, lock, or ownership transfer.

direct_reference_scan.result: Exactly five direct instruction references to the four root words: one each for DAT_0167eae0, DAT_0167eb60, DAT_0167eb0c, and two for DAT_0167eae4. All are reads. No direct write xref or direct equality operand was found.

accessor_xref_summary.0x00b3d3a0: direct global read only; one executable thunk call path through 0x00b5ca50

direct_reference_scan.interpretation: This closes the direct-reference surface for the four words. It does not close indirect or runtime publication.

root_word_literal_results: Pattern e4 ea 67 01 matched only 0x00b3d2a1 and 0x00b3d2f2.
literal_and_table_scan.exact_accessor_data_table_search: No exact data-byte occurrence was found for the four accessor entry addresses 0x00b3d300, 0x00b3d400, 0x00b3d2a0, or 0x00b3d3a0.
literal_and_table_scan.star_thunk_table_reference: 0x00b5ca50 is a data-referenced thunk at 0x0146286c. Its bytes are CALL 0x00b3d3a0; MOV EDX,[EAX]; MOV ECX,EAX; MOV EAX,[EDX+0x28]; JMP EAX. This is a vtable/dispatch consumer of the canonical star getter, not a write to DAT_0167eb0c and not a root publication table.

base_table_separator.result: 0x00b3cf40 initializes/reads only twelve float words at offsets 0x00..0x2c. 0x00b3ce80, 0x00b3cec0, and 0x00b3cf00 read float fields in that range. No access at the arithmetic offsets corresponding to the four root words was found. The base-table publication hypothesis is rejected for this candidate.
base_table_separator.limit: Other opaque base, index, or bulk mechanisms are not ruled out.

computed_scan.scope: Concrete P-code constants and arithmetic for COPY, INT_ADD, INT_SUB, INT_MULT, INT_AND, INT_OR, INT_XOR, PTRSUB, PTRADD, and casts, with STORE address propagation.
computed_scan.interpretation: No concrete arithmetic address or P-code STORE was resolved to any of the four target words. This is a bounded negative observation, not proof of absence; opaque pointer-derived addresses, external writes, unresolved code, and runtime/loader writes remain open.

accessor_pair_and_equality_scan.noun_pair: 0x00b3d300 and 0x00b3d400 are called by 11 recovered functions: 0x00ae9f50, 0x00aebe90, 0x00b33350, 0x00b335d0, 0x00cd3bf0, 0x00d0e170, 0x00d100b0, 0x00d38150, 0x00ef10c0, 0x00fe5a20, and 0x01007430.
accessor_pair_and_equality_scan.noun_pair_interpretation: The co-call set does not establish equality. The inspected bodies use the accessors in separate noun/data/lifecycle operations, mode branches, or separate receiver paths. 0x00cd3bf0 retains the canonical result in a local while the alternate accessor is used in a different condition/path; 0x00b335d0 has separate mode branches. No explicit cross-accessor pointer comparison was recovered.
accessor_pair_and_equality_scan.star_pair_interpretation: No static equality or co-call separator was found; the canonical star getter is reached through the 0x00b5ca50 thunk/data reference and the alternate star accessor is used in a separate high-fan-in path.
accessor_pair_and_equality_scan.equality_conclusion: Pointer equality cannot be closed. Shared consumer topology is not an equality proof.

receiver_chain.consumer_window: 0x00bff2d0 calls 0x01002bd0 at 0x00bff3ad, moves the result to ECX at 0x00bff3b2, and calls 0x00b1fdb0 at 0x00bff3b4.
receiver_chain.construction: 0x00fda750 allocates a 0xf0 parent and stores the constructed child at parent+0x15c. 0x010066e0 constructs the parent, stores it in DAT_016dc0fc, allocates a 0x108 child, constructs it, and stores that child at parent+0x30.
receiver_chain.teardown: 0x01006880 clears DAT_016dc0fc after releasing the child at parent+0x30. 0x010077c0 is the conditional parent destructor/free path in the inspected lifecycle.
receiver_chain.conclusion: DAT_016dc0fc is a separately published parent/context root with direct lifecycle coverage. The 0x00bff2d0 receiver is not DAT_0167eae0 or DAT_0167eb60, and its +0x54 result must not be relabeled as either noun slot. The receiver chain does not prove noun/star root aliasing.

star_manager: 0x00b60d80 allocates/constructs and registers a cStarManager-shaped object and reaches 0x00bae490; no direct target-word xref occurs.
0x00bae490 initializes manager-owned fields including mEmpires +0x150 and relationship field +0x204; no direct target-word xref occurs.
0x00bb6a30 initializes the relationship manager at +0x204 and other manager state; no direct target-word xref occurs.
0x00bb7250 tears down manager state and clears/releases +0x204; no direct target-word xref occurs.
0x00babe70 releases manager-owned maps and fields; no direct target-word xref occurs.
noun_records: 0x00b21410 unlinks a noun map node, releases its payload, frees the node, and clears a matching owner field; no direct target-word xref occurs.
0x00b25fe0 performs noun-related data cleanup and record traversal; no direct target-word xref occurs.
constructor_and_teardown_observations.lifecycle_conclusion: The inspected manager and record lifecycle paths are real but do not publish, clear, or alias the four target words directly. This does not rule out a separate opaque service-registration or phase-publication path.

storage_and_aliasing.physical_storage: The four target addresses are four distinct four-byte words. Physical aliasing of those storage locations is rejected.
storage_and_aliasing.value_aliasing: The same object pointer could still be written into two or more words by an unobserved common publisher, phase rebinding, or external/runtime mechanism. No such publisher or equality observation was recovered.
storage_and_aliasing.noun_storage: The noun data path is receiver-owned: 0x00b21340 reads mNouns at receiver+0x78 and mNounMap at receiver+0x98. The accessor load itself does not share or transfer storage.
storage_and_aliasing.star_storage: The empire map is manager-owned at cStarManager+0x150; relationship state is field-owned at +0x204. Accessor loads do not establish cross-slot storage sharing.
storage_and_aliasing.aliasing_mechanism: No indirection table, handle, proxy, shared map root, AddRef-on-access, or direct alias store was found for the four target words. Generic indirect publication remains possible.

hypotheses.claim: DAT_0167eae0 and DAT_0167eb60 always contain the same cGameNounManager pointer.
predictions: A common writer, equality check, bulk publication, or unpublication path would relate both words.
The 11 noun co-call functions would contain a cross-accessor equality operation or a common receiver assignment.
supporting_evidence: Both accessors are raw noun-manager-shaped loads and noun consumers use both paths.
evidence_against: The words are distinct, have only read xrefs, and no common writer or equality operand was found.
Co-call functions use the accessors in separate paths; no cross-accessor comparison was recovered.

hypotheses.claim: DAT_0167eae4 and DAT_0167eb0c always contain the same cStarManager pointer.
predictions: A common writer, equality check, or phase-independent publication would relate both words.
A live consumer would call both star accessors or otherwise compare their returned values.
supporting_evidence: Both accessors are raw manager-shaped loads and the canonical accessor is SDK-named cStarManager::Get.
evidence_against: The words are distinct and have no direct writer or equality xref.
No recovered function co-calls the two star accessors; the canonical path is sparse and thunk-mediated.

hypotheses.claim: A common computed, table-driven, or bulk publisher fills one or more target words.
predictions: A concrete arithmetic address, P-code STORE, exact table slot, or opaque bulk copy would reach a target word.
The publisher would be connected to manager construction, registration, or phase entry.
supporting_evidence: Direct writers are absent, so any live publication model needs an indirect mechanism.
The receiver root demonstrates that separate service-root publication exists elsewhere in the binary.
evidence_against: The bounded computed scan resolved zero target addresses and zero computed stores.
Exact target-word byte scans found only accessor instructions, and the tested 0x0167ea80 base is a float block rather than a manager table.

hypotheses.claim: The noun and/or star slots are phase-specific, independently rebound, or hold distinct manager instances.
predictions: A transition would update one slot without updating the other.
One or both slots could be null or different during a phase window.
A manager/map/relationship teardown could occur independently of the global slot.
supporting_evidence: The slots are physically distinct raw words with different direct consumer topology.
Manager construction and teardown are field/service-oriented and do not directly publish the target words.
evidence_against: No direct or bounded computed rebind path was recovered.
No runtime phase observation was performed.

hypotheses.claim: One slot is obsolete or unpublished in the exercised modes while the other is the live port.
predictions: The sparse canonical path would be dead, null, or limited to an unowned thunk while the alternate serves gameplay.
supporting_evidence: DAT_0167eb0c has only one executable getter reference through 0x00b5ca50 and one data reference at 0x0146286c.
DAT_0167eae4 has high-fan-in consumers and feeds the current-player lookup path.
evidence_against: The canonical getter is still present in a data-referenced dispatch thunk and cannot be declared dead from fan-in alone.

hypotheses.claim: DAT_016dc0fc/0x01002bd0 is the common publication root for the noun or star slots.
predictions: The receiver chain would feed one of the four target accessors or write one of the four target words.
The receiver's constructor/teardown would explain target publication/unpublication.
supporting_evidence: DAT_016dc0fc has direct constructor and teardown writes and is a real published parent/context root.
evidence_against: 0x01002bd0 reads DAT_016dc0fc, while 0x00bff2d0 moves that result to ECX and calls 0x00b1fdb0; it is not a call to b3d300 or b3d400.
DAT_016dc0fc is a distinct global with its own direct write/read surface and no direct target-word xref.

hypotheses.claim: The four target words share storage or a handle/proxy mechanism.
predictions: A memory alias, proxy field, indirection table, or shared owner would be visible in the root/accessor path.
evidence_against: The four storage locations are distinct four-byte words and all accessors are direct raw loads.
No indirection, proxy, AddRef-on-access, or alias-store mechanism was found.

hypotheses.claim: The inspected manager constructors and destructors directly publish or clear all four target roots.
predictions: The cStarManager and noun-record lifecycle functions would contain direct target-word writes or equality operations.
supporting_evidence: The inspected cStarManager and noun-record lifecycle functions are substantial and perform field-level ownership work.
evidence_against: The target-word xref inventory contains no direct writers; the inspected lifecycle functions operate on manager fields, maps, relationship state, and records instead.

hypotheses.claim: 0x00b3d300 is a noun-manager-compatible alternate accessor rather than a generic context locator.
predictions: Its result should be accepted by the noun receiver/data path, including mNouns and mNounMap field use.
supporting_evidence: 0x00bff2d0 calls 0x00b3d300 and passes the result through ECX to the noun-data path.

separating_observations.name: direct-root-reference-surface
separating_observations.result: Five direct reads and zero direct writes across the four target words; no direct equality operand.
separating_observations.decision: Separates distinct storage and direct accessor mechanics from publication/liveness claims, but does not prove immutability.

separating_observations.name: literal-table-surface
separating_observations.result: Exact target literals occur only in accessor instructions; no exact target-word table slot was found. One star-getter thunk is data-referenced at 0x0146286c.
separating_observations.decision: Rejects the inspected exact-table publisher while preserving opaque bulk/table mechanisms.

separating_observations.name: bounded-computed-store-surface
separating_observations.result: Zero concrete computed target addresses and zero computed target stores.
separating_observations.decision: No concrete arithmetic publisher is identified; the scan is not exhaustive for opaque or runtime writers.

separating_observations.name: accessor-pair-surface
separating_observations.result: Eleven noun co-call functions; zero star co-call functions. Inspected noun co-call bodies show separate use paths, not equality.
separating_observations.decision: Co-call topology does not close pointer equality.

separating_observations.name: receiver-provenance-surface
separating_observations.result: 0x01002bd0 returns DAT_016dc0fc; 0x00bff2d0 passes that value to 0x00b1fdb0, while DAT_016dc0fc has its own constructor/teardown.
separating_observations.decision: Rejects treating the receiver as either noun-slot root and narrows its identity to a distinct parent/context publication.

separating_observations.name: manager-and-record-lifecycle-surface
separating_observations.result: Inspected star manager construction/init/shutdown/destructor and noun map/record cleanup do not directly touch the four target words.
separating_observations.decision: Record teardown is not root unpublication; separate opaque publication paths remain open.

separating_observations.name: runtime-equality-and-phase-observation
separating_observations.result: Not performed under the read-only and excluded-game-directory constraints.
separating_observations.decision: Permanent equality, phase rebinding, distinct instances, and obsolete/unpublished alternatives remain runtime-open.

closed: One distinct receiver publication chain for DAT_016dc0fc
No direct or bounded concrete writer for the four roots

unresolved_slot_level_obligations.explanation: The minimum exact count is per root word and per pair. A single opaque function could publish or clear multiple words, so the number of concrete writer functions is not bounded by these counts. At least four root publication states, four root unpublication/teardown states, and two cross-slot equality relations remain unresolved.

exact_lower_bound.not_a_closed_result: Pointer equality/publication cannot be closed. The defensible interim boundary is four separate opaque root handles with explicit lifecycle contracts; do not merge noun slots, merge star slots, or route DAT_016dc0fc through them.

minimum_safe_model: Keep DAT_0167eae0 and DAT_0167eb60 as separate raw noun-root ports until equality is observed.
Keep DAT_0167eae4 and DAT_0167eb0c as separate raw star-root ports until equality is observed.
Treat the noun map/list and star empire map as receiver-owned storage; do not infer cross-port storage sharing from a common accessor name or co-call.
Keep publication, replacement, and unpublication as explicit lifecycle events even though their current indirect mechanism is unresolved.
Keep DAT_016dc0fc/0x01002bd0 as a separate parent/context receiver path.
unsafe_to_assume: The 0x0167ea80 float block is a manager-root table.
A data-referenced getter thunk publishes a root word.
The receiver chain's +0x54 result is the canonical noun manager.
No indirect writer exists merely because direct, literal, and bounded computed scans found none.

limitations: No runtime pointer equality, phase, or teardown trace was performed.
No runtime evidence can be inferred from zero bytes in the loaded static image.
No direct or bounded computed writer is not proof that no indirect writer exists.
The exact pointer owner and publication timing for the four noun/star roots remain unresolved.
